plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, fragrant mounds send up slender spikes of tiny violet-blue flowers. In the south of France they ripple across the hills in long, perfumed rows that hum with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer. In Provence, flowering usually begins in mid-June and peaks in early July.
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: This is South Africa's national flower. Its flower head is as wide as a dinner plate, with a crown of silky, pointed bracts that fade from blush pink to deep rose around a downy center.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn through spring in the Southern Hemisphere. June falls in the Cape winter, when many plants are in flower.
plants.location: Fynbos shrublands of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas are an ancient plant family that dates back to when the southern continents were joined. The genus is named after Proteus, the shape-shifting Greek sea god, because the plants vary so much in form.

plants.name: Rhododendron catawbiense
plants.description: Rounded shrubs on high Appalachian balds burst into huge clusters of lilac-purple, bell-shaped flowers. Whole mountaintops glow magenta against the evergreen leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June is the peak at high elevations, with flowering running from late May to early July.
plants.location: Southern Appalachian Mountains, such as Roan Mountain on the North Carolina–Tennessee border, USA
plants.funFact: This wild species is a parent of many of the hardy rhododendron hybrids grown in cold-climate gardens around the world.
